$comment: Datasets are PINNED, not vendored: the harness fetches by URL and refuses to run if the sha256 does not
match. Redistributing somebody else's dataset inside this repository would put us in the business of
hosting it, and a copy is one more thing that can drift from what the authors publish.
Every count here was MEASURED FROM THE FILE, not taken from a paper. The protocol requires that, and the
first pin already shows why: the dialogue is roughly twice the size a published summary suggested, which
moves the full-context control's cost more than anything else in the run.

locomo.licence: TO CONFIRM before publishing any result — read the repository's LICENSE and the paper's terms, and record the answer here rather than assuming a permissive default.

dialogueTokensApprox.$method: characters / 4, the usual English approximation. Replace with a real tokenizer count at harness time — this is for sizing the run, not for a published figure.

$comment: The release labels categories by NUMBER, not by name. The mapping to the paper's names
(single-hop / multi-hop / temporal / open-domain / adversarial) MUST be confirmed against the
paper and the repository's own evaluation code before any per-category result is published.
It matters more than it looks: one code is 22.5% of the whole set, so if that is the adversarial
category then dropping it — the thing published comparisons are most often accused of — removes
nearly a quarter of the questions rather than a rounding error.

longmemeval.url: TO PIN — Tier 2. Not fetched yet.

models.$comment: Pinned before the first run. A run that cannot get a pinned model must FAIL rather than substitute one — a benchmark that quietly swaps the judge is not measuring what its results claim.

embedding.id: the instance's own local model, in-process via @huggingface/transformers
embedding.$comment: No API cost and no network. Recorded because 'which embedder' is a real variable and leaving it implicit would make the run unreproducible.
